rounds.text: The company is fundamentally undervalued [E6, E7], trading at a P/E of 19.57x [E6] and a P/B of 2.35x [E7], both of which sit below their respective sector benchmarks [E6, E7]. This discount is further highlighted by a discounted cash flow analysis that places the company's intrinsic value at Rs 365 [E44], providing a 20.3% margin of safety [E45] relative to the current market price of Rs 291 [E44]. While historical growth has been modest [E16, E20], recent performance indicates a significant acceleration, with trailing twelve-month sales growth of 17% [E17] and a recent year-over-year quarterly net profit surge of 49% [E68]. The business operates with superior efficiency compared to its peers [E8, E10], maintaining an ROCE of 15.6% [E12] and an ROA of 9.5% against a sector benchmark of 6.59% [E8], all while remaining conservatively financed with zero debt [E37, E58]. Market sentiment is exceptionally strong, as evidenced by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E50] and positive institutional money flow [E43]. Conceded: [E36], [E64], the company faces challenges with negative free cash flow of Rs -23 Cr [E36] and an increase in working capital days to 187 [E64]. Despite these operational hurdles, the company's rules-based screen score of 88 out of 100 [E65] suggests that its accelerating profit growth [E68, E69] and robust dividend payout of 26.2% [E60] are being under-appreciated by the broader market [E44, E65].

Despite a clean balance sheet with zero borrowings [E37], Mazda Ltd carries severe operational and fundamental risks that undermine its current valuation. Most alarmingly, the company experienced severe cash burn in March 2026, generating a negative operating cash flow of Rs -19 Cr and a negative free cash flow of Rs -23 Cr, resulting in an abysmal cash conversion ratio of -0.68x [E34, E35, E36]. This cash drain is compounded by deteriorating working capital efficiency, as debtor days stretched from 77.4 to 102 days and overall working capital days bloated from 125 days to 187 days [E63, E64]. Furthermore, long-term growth has been remarkably sluggish, marked by a poor 3-year compounded sales growth of 3% and a negligible 3-year profit growth of 1% [E16, E20], leading to explicit warnings of poor 5-year sales growth [E61] and low 3-year return on equity averaging 12.7% [E62]. Operating margins have also compressed over the trailing twelve months down to 16% compared to 18% three years prior, accompanied by an inconsistent margin trend [E30, E32]. Conceded: the stock trades below its DCF-derived intrinsic value and carries positive short-term momentum with an institutional money flow [E43, E44, E70]. However, high annualised volatility of 44.1% and a punishing historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -60.2% highlight the substantial downside risks masking the headline valuation [E52, E53].

Conceded: [E34, E35, E36, E63, E64]. However, the bear overstates long-term fundamental risk by ignoring the sharp positive acceleration in recent performance, including a 17% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a robust 11% profit growth over the same period [E17, E21]. Furthermore, recent quarterly momentum points directly upward, with operating margins expanding by 3 percentage points to 9% in June 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E31], alongside expectations for a good upcoming quarter [E59]. The company's pristine balance sheet with zero borrowings [E37, E38] provides ample financial flexibility to navigate working capital fluctuations while maintaining a healthy dividend payout of 26.2% [E60]. Finally, the market price offers a tangible margin of safety of 20.3% below its DCF intrinsic value [E44, E45], backed by a rules-based screen score of 88 out of 100 [E65] and a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E50].

Conceded: [E17, E21, E31, E59, E60]. While recent trailing numbers show growth, the bull overlooks the severe structural stagnation across multi-year horizons, such as 3-year sales growth of 3% and 3-year profit growth of a negligible 1% [E16, E20]. The bull dismisses working capital and cash generation issues, yet operating cash flow plunged to negative Rs 19 Cr and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 23 Cr for March 2026, resulting in an alarming cash conversion ratio of -0.68x [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, debtor days have severely worsened from 77.4 to 102 days, and overall working capital days have ballooned from 125 days to 187 days [E63, E64]. The bull's reliance on a valuation model and relative strength ignores historical volatility, where the stock has suffered a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -60.2% alongside an annualized volatility of 44.1% [E52, E53].

Conceded: [E16, E20, E34, E35, E36, E63, E64]. While multi-year figures show softer periods and working capital stretched, the bear ignores the sharp inflection in top-line growth with a trailing twelve-month sales surge of 17% [E17] and recent quarterly sales jumping 62% year-over-year [E66]. The company operates with essentially zero debt at 0.00x debt-to-equity and Rs 0 Cr in borrowings, providing immense balance sheet resilience to absorb working capital cycles [E37, E38]. Furthermore, the bear's anxiety over valuation and historical drawdowns is neutralized by fundamental outperformance, including an ROA of 9.5% and ROCE of 14.99% that both outpace sector benchmarks [E8, E10], alongside a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 [E50]. Finally, the DCF model firmly indicates intrinsic value lies at Rs 365 per share—offering a clear 20.3% margin of safety from the current price—while the reverse DCF demonstrates that the market is currently pricing in only 7.9% earnings growth against the 11.0% base case [E44, E45, E46].

The bull's reliance on a 17% trailing twelve-month sales surge and a 62% quarterly jump ignores the severe structural decay underpinning multi-year performance, including a sluggish 3-year sales growth of 3% [E16] and a pathetic 3-year profit growth of 1% [E20]. Zero debt [E37] does not fix the alarming operational reality that cash conversion has collapsed to -0.68x, accompanied by negative operating cash flow of Rs -19 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -23 Cr in Mar 2026 [E34, E35, E36]. The bull cites outperforming ROA [E8] and ROCE [E10], but glosses over the deterioration in operating margin from 18% down to 16% [E30] and the ballooning of debtor days from 77.4 to 102 days alongside working capital days blowing out from 125 to 187 days [E63, E64]. Finally, pointing to a DCF margin of safety [E44, E45] is hollow when the stock has a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -60.2% [E52], a high annualised volatility of 44.1% [E53], and a price-led divergence where 5-year share price growth of 19% vastly outpaces 5-year profit growth of 11% [E19, E23, E55].
